metadata.title: Password field
metadata.description: The password field component securely collects sensitive information from users. Use password field for password entry, where input characters are automatically masked for privacy.

properties.type: "on" | "off" | PasswordAutocompleteField | `section-${string} current-password` | `section-${string} new-password` | "shipping current-password" | "shipping new-password" | "billing current-password" | "billing new-password" | `section-${string} shipping current-password` | `section-${string} shipping new-password` | `section-${string} billing current-password` | `section-${string} billing new-password`
properties.description: A hint as to the intended content of the field. When set to on (the default), this property indicates that the field should support autofill, but you do not have any more semantic information on the intended contents. When set to off, you are indicating that this field contains sensitive information, or contents that are never saved, like one-time codes. Alternatively, you can provide value which describes the specific data you would like to be entered into this field during autofill.

The initial value of the field when it first loads. Unlike placeholder, this is a real value that the user can edit and that gets submitted with the form. Once the user starts typing, their input replaces it. Changing this property after the field has loaded has no effect. To update the field value at any time, use value instead.

Supplementary text displayed below the field to provide additional context, instructions, or help. Use this to clarify the expected input or provide guidance to users. This text is announced to screen readers.
Whether the field is disabled, preventing any user interaction.
An error message displayed below the field to indicate validation problems. When set, the field is styled with error indicators and the message is announced to screen readers.
A unique identifier for the element. Use this to reference the element in JavaScript, link labels to form controls, or target specific elements for styling or scripting.

The text displayed as the field label, which identifies the purpose of the field to users. This label is associated with the field for accessibility and helps users understand what information to provide.

Controls whether the label is visible to all users or only to screen readers. visible: The label is shown to everyone (default).exclusive: The label is visually hidden but still announced by screen readers. Use exclusive when the surrounding context makes the label redundant visually, but screen reader users still need it for clarity.
The maximum number of characters allowed in the field.
The minimum number of characters required in the field.
The name attribute for the field, used to identify the field's value when the form is submitted. Must be unique within the nearest containing form.
The placeholder text displayed in the field when it's empty, providing a hint about the expected input format or value.
Whether the field is read-only and can't be edited. Read-only fields remain focusable and their content is announced by screen readers.

Whether the field requires a value before form submission. Displays a visual indicator and adds semantic meaning, but doesn't automatically validate or show errors. Use the error property to display validation messages.
The current value for the field. If omitted, the field will be empty.

examples.name: Main example
examples.html_code:
<s-password-field
  label="Password"
  placeholder="Enter your password"
  details="Must be at least 8 characters long"
  minLength="8"
></s-password-field>
examples.erb_code: <%= form.password_field :password, label: "Password", placeholder: "Enter your password", details: "Must be at least 8 characters long", minlength: "8" %>

examples.name: Collect a password
examples.description: Securely collect sensitive credentials from users. This example pairs a label with masked input.
examples.html_code:
<s-password-field
  label="Password"
  placeholder="Enter your password"
  details="Must be at least 8 characters long"
  minLength="8"
></s-password-field>
examples.erb_code: <%= form.password_field :password, label: "Password", placeholder: "Enter your password", details: "Must be at least 8 characters long", minlength: "8" %>

examples.name: Set validation rules
examples.description: Enforce password requirements before submission. This example configures a required field with minimum length validation and autocomplete for new passwords.
examples.erb_code: <%= form.password_field :password, label: "Password", required: true, minlength: "8", autocomplete: "new-password" %>

examples.name: Show validation errors
examples.description: Communicate password problems clearly to users. This example displays an error message when the password doesn't meet length requirements.
examples.html_code:
<s-password-field
  label="Password"
  name="password"
  error="Password must be at least 8 characters"
  minLength="8"
  autocomplete="new-password"
></s-password-field>
examples.erb_code: <%= form.password_field :password, label: "Password", error: "Password must be at least 8 characters", minlength: "8", autocomplete: "new-password" %>

examples.name: Add helper text
examples.description: Help users understand password requirements upfront. This example adds helper text beneath the field explaining what makes a valid password.
examples.html_code:
<s-password-field
  label="Create password"
  name="new-password"
  details="Password must be at least 8 characters and include uppercase, lowercase, and numbers"
  minLength="8"
  autocomplete="new-password"
></s-password-field>
examples.erb_code: <%= form.password_field :new_password, label: "Create password", details: "Password must be at least 8 characters and include uppercase, lowercase, and numbers", minlength: "8", autocomplete: "new-password" %>

examples.name: Build a login form
examples.description: Create a complete authentication form. This example combines a password field with an email field for login or registration.
examples.html_code:
<s-stack gap="base">
  <s-email-field
    label="Email"
    name="email"
    autocomplete="email"
    required
  ></s-email-field>
  <s-password-field
    label="Password"
    name="password"
    autocomplete="current-password"
    required
  ></s-password-field>
</s-stack>
examples.erb_code:
<s-stack gap="base">
  <%= form.email_field :email, label: "Email", autocomplete: "email", required: true %>
  <%= form.password_field :password, label: "Password", autocomplete: "current-password", required: true %>
</s-stack>

examples.name: Display a requirement checklist
examples.description: Display a password requirements checklist alongside the field. This example lists requirements like character length and case requirements.
examples.html_code:
<s-stack gap="large-100">
  <s-password-field
    label="Create password"
    name="password"
    value="example-password"
    autocomplete="new-password"
    required
  ></s-password-field>
  <s-stack gap="small-200">
    <s-text tone="success">✓ At least 8 characters</s-text>
    <s-text color="subdued">○ Contains uppercase letter</s-text>
    <s-text color="subdued">○ Contains lowercase letter</s-text>
    <s-text color="subdued">○ Contains number</s-text>
  </s-stack>
</s-stack>
examples.erb_code:
<s-stack gap="large-100">
  <%= form.password_field :password, label: "Create password", value: "example-password", autocomplete: "new-password", required: true %>
  <s-stack gap="small-200">
    <s-text tone="success">✓ At least 8 characters</s-text>
    <s-text color="subdued">○ Contains uppercase letter</s-text>
    <s-text color="subdued">○ Contains lowercase letter</s-text>
    <s-text color="subdued">○ Contains number</s-text>
  </s-stack>
</s-stack>
